Pitfall: P07: Merging different concepts in the same class.

Explanation: OOPS! raises this pitfall when a class name contains a conjunction such as ``and'' or ``or''. It was raised for the afmo:RaceOrEthnicity and eo:SafetyAndPerformanceExplanation classes. afmo:RaceOrEthnicity was modelled as a single concept by design, since race and ethnicity are often defined and used ambiguously (see Hunt and Megyesi (2008)). eo:SafetyAndPerformanceExplanation is reused from the Explanation Ontology. The class name was retained to preserve alignment with the original ontology.

Pitfall: P22: Using different naming conventions in the ontology.

Explanation: Due to the re-use of concepts from other ontologies, some of the classes and properties in the PHMO use different naming conventions. Original PHMO classes use TitleCase for classes (e.g. MonitoredPerson) and camelCase for object and data properties (e.g. hasAgeGroup). Other imported ontologies have different naming conventions, such as the use of underscores and numeric codes in the Evidence and Conclusion Ontology (e.g. "ECO_0000000" for "Evidence").

Ontology Specification Draft

Abstract

The AFMO is a condition-specific extension of the Personal Health Monitoring Ontology (PHMO) for AI-based atrial fibrillation (AF) monitoring applications. It supports the representation of AF risk factors, AF risk assessments, AF episodes and their predictions, ECG data, AF comorbidities, and AF-related interventions.

Introduction back to ToC

The AFMO is an ontology for AI-based monitoring of atrial fibrillation (AF). It extends the [Personal Health Monitoring Ontology (PHMO)](https://mbithenzomo.github.io/phmo/), a reusable general ontology for AI-based personal health monitoring applications. The PHMO defines how personal health monitoring concepts are modelled. The AFMO defines which concepts are modelled for AF. The AFMO supports three main functionalities for AF: AF risk assessment, AF episode prediction, and intervention recommendation. AF risk is assessed by a hybrid Bayesian network, using risk factors such as age group, comorbidities, ECG characteristics, and lifestyle factors. AF episodes are predicted from ECG observations by a deep neural network. The expected utility of recommended interventions, such as alcoholism counselling or angiotensin receptor blocker therapy, is calculated by a Bayesian decision network. Each output is linked to the model that generated it, the inputs it was based on, and the datasets used to train and test the model. AF risk relationships and interventions are also linked to supporting scientific evidence, such as clinical guidelines and systematic reviews.

AFMO: Description back to ToC

The AFMO extends the Personal Health Monitoring Ontology (PHMO) with concepts specific to atrial fibrillation (AF) monitoring. From version 3.0, general personal health monitoring concepts have moved to the PHMO (http://purl.org/phmo), which the AFMO imports. Terms listed as deleted in the changelog have moved to the PHMO namespace. In addition to the ontologies reused through the PHMO, the AFMO contains concepts reused from the following ontologies: - Human Disease Ontology (DO) - Medical Action Ontology (MAxO) Health domain concepts have been manually cross-referenced to concepts from the Unified Medical Language System (UMLS) metathesaurus, which maps to several medical vocabularies and terminologies, including: - SNOMED CT (US) - Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) Thesaurus - National Cancer Institute (NCI) Thesaurus - MedlinePlus

Contrastive explanationc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://purl.org/heals/eo#ContrastiveExplanation

Answers the question “Why this output instead of that output,” making a contrast between the given output and the facts that led to it (inputs and other considerations), and an alternate output of interest and the foil (facts that would have led to it).
scope note
Is there a ‘system recommendation’ that was made (let’s call it A)? What facts led to it? Is there another ‘system recommendation’ that could have happened or did occur, (let’s call it B)? What was the ‘foil’ that led to B? Can A and B be compared?
Is defined by
https://purl.org/heals/eo
Source
Chari, S., Seneviratne, O., Ghalwash, M., Shirai, S., Gruen, D. M., Meyer, P., Chakraborty, P., & McGuinness, D. L. (2024). Explanation Ontology: A general-purpose, semantic representation for supporting user-centered explanations. Semantic Web. https://doi.org/10.3233/SW-233282
Example
Why choose option A over option B that I typically choose?
has super-classes
Explanation c
has members
AF risk explanation 4 ni

Counterfactual explanationc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://purl.org/heals/eo#CounterfactualExplanation

Addresses the question of what solutions would have been obtained with a different set of inputs than those used.
scope note
Is there a different set of inputs that can be considered? If so what is the alternate ‘system recommendation’?
Is defined by
https://purl.org/heals/eo
Source
Chari, S., Seneviratne, O., Ghalwash, M., Shirai, S., Gruen, D. M., Meyer, P., Chakraborty, P., & McGuinness, D. L. (2024). Explanation Ontology: A general-purpose, semantic representation for supporting user-centered explanations. Semantic Web. https://doi.org/10.3233/SW-233282
Example
What if input A was over 1000?
has super-classes
Explanation c
has members
AF risk explanation 3 ni

Data explanationc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://purl.org/heals/eo#DataExplanation

Focuses on what the data is and how it has been used in a particular decision, as well as what data and how it has been used to train and test the ML model. This type of explanation can help users understand the influence of data on decisions.
scope note
Is there a ‘system recommendation’ from an ‘AI method’ that has as input, a ‘dataset’ or part of it? Is there a ‘system recommendation’ that includes ‘object records’ that are used to train / test the ‘AI method’?
Is defined by
https://purl.org/heals/eo
Source
Chari, S., Seneviratne, O., Ghalwash, M., Shirai, S., Gruen, D. M., Meyer, P., Chakraborty, P., & McGuinness, D. L. (2024). Explanation Ontology: A general-purpose, semantic representation for supporting user-centered explanations. Semantic Web. https://doi.org/10.3233/SW-233282

How has the data been used to train the ML model?
How it has been used in a particular decision?
What the data is?

Observationc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/Observation

Act of carrying out an (Observation) Procedure to estimate or calculate a value of a property of a FeatureOfInterest. Links to a Sensor to describe what made the Observation and how; links to an ObservableProperty to describe what the result is an estimate of, and to a FeatureOfInterest to detail what that property was associated with.
act of carrying out an ObservingProcedure using a Sensor to estimate or calculate a value of an observable Property of a FeatureOfInterest
scope note
An Observation primarily concerns a single Property of a single FeatureOfInterest. Observations of multiple properties, or other combinations of Observations, may be described in an ObservationCollection. Alternatively, applications may choose to encapsulate complexity by defining a complex property with multiple individual components, and a corresponding complex result (e.g., a vector). This approach is not prohibited by the SSN Ontology, but the details are beyond the scope of SSN.
Is defined by
http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/
http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/obs/
Example
The activity of estimating the intensity of an Earthquake using the Mercalli intensity scale is an Observation as is measuring the moment magnitude, i.e., the energy released by said earthquake.
has super-classes
has sub-classes
Continuous observation c, Discrete observation c

Observation collectionc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/ObservationCollection

set of Observations or ObservationCollections; collections may be nested All Observation properties may appear in an Observation Collection, including: hasFeatureOfInterest , hasUltimateFeatureOfInterest , usedProcedure , madeBySensor , observedProperty , phenomenonTime , startTime, resultTime , hasResult , hasSimpleResult : If they are present, the value of these properties summarize the values of the matching properties of the member observations, where membership is either direct or transitive through one or more member observation collections. The following consistency rules apply with respect to the Observation properties listed above: 1. Where an individual Observation Collection omits a property, a member Observation (direct or transitive) MAY have any value for that property. 2. Where an individual Observation Collection has a single value for a property, each member Observation(direct or transitive) MUST have that same value for the property - i.e., the collection is homogeneous in that property. That property MAY then be omitted in any member Observation or Observation Collection. 3. Where an individual Observation Collection has more than one value for a property, each member Observation (direct or transitive) MUST have a value for that property that matches one of the values for the property in the collection. 4. Where an individual Observation Collection has a value for a property that is a range or interval, each member Observation (direct or transitive) MUST have a value for that property that matches or falls within that range or interval. 5. Where an individual Observation Collection has more than one value for a property that is a range or interval, each member Observation (direct or transitive) MUST have a value for that property that either matches or falls within one of those ranges or intervals.
set of Observations or ObservationCollections; collections may be nested All Observation properties may appear in an Observation Collection, including: hasFeatureOfInterest , hasUltimateFeatureOfInterest , usedProcedure , madeBySensor , observedProperty , phenomenonTime , startTime, resultTime , hasResult , hasSimpleResult : If they are present, the value of these properties summarize the values of the matching properties of the member observations, where membership is either direct or transitive through one or more member observation collections. Rationale explanationc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://purl.org/heals/eo#RationaleExplanation

About the “why” of an ML decision and provides reasons that led to a decision, and is delivered in an accessible and understandable way, especially for lay users. If the ML decision was not what users expected, rationale explanations allows users to assess whether they believe the reasoning of the decision is flawed. While, if so, the explanation supports them to formulate reasonable arguments for why they think this is the case.
scope note
Is there a ‘system recommendation’ from an ‘AI method’ that has a ‘system trace’? Is there a ‘local explanation’ output that an ‘explanation’ is based on?
Is defined by
https://purl.org/heals/eo
Source
Chari, S., Seneviratne, O., Ghalwash, M., Shirai, S., Gruen, D. M., Meyer, P., Chakraborty, P., & McGuinness, D. L. (2024). Explanation Ontology: A general-purpose, semantic representation for supporting user-centered explanations. Semantic Web. https://doi.org/10.3233/SW-233282
Example
Why was this ML decision made and provide reasons that led to a decision?
has super-classes
Explanation c
has members
AF episode explanation 1 ni, AF risk explanation 1 ni, Intervention explanation 3 ni

A scholarly work that surveys the state of the art of topics central to a particular subject or relating to a specific domain (e.g. the scope of a certain journal or conference). Papers of this kind may contain a selective bibliography listing key papers related to the subject or providing advice on information sources, or they may strive to be comprehensive, covering all contributions to the development of a topic and exploring their different findings or views. E.g. see http://www.emeraldgrouppublishing.com/products/journals/author_guidelines.htm?id=JD
has super-classes
Review c

Safety and performance explanationc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://purl.org/heals/eo#SafetyAndPerformanceExplanation

Deals with steps taken across the design and implementation of an ML system to maximise the accuracy, reliability, security, and robustness of its decisions and behaviours. Safety and performance explanations help to assure individuals that an ML system is safe and reliable by explanation to test and monitor the accuracy, reliability, security, and robustness of the ML model.
scope note
Is there a ‘system recommendation’ from an ‘AI method’ that is part of a ‘system’ that exposes its design ‘plans’? Is there a ‘system recommendation’ that includes ‘object records’ that are used to train / test the ‘AI method’?
Is defined by
https://purl.org/heals/eo
Source
Chari, S., Seneviratne, O., Ghalwash, M., Shirai, S., Gruen, D. M., Meyer, P., Chakraborty, P., & McGuinness, D. L. (2024). Explanation Ontology: A general-purpose, semantic representation for supporting user-centered explanations. Semantic Web. https://doi.org/10.3233/SW-233282
Example
How has the data been used to train the ML model?
What steps were taken to ensure robustness and reliability of AI method?
What steps were taken to ensure robustness and reliability of system?
What were the plans for the system development?
has super-classes
Explanation c
has sub-classes
Data explanation c
has members
AF risk explanation 2 ni

References the results of rigorous scientific methods, observations, and measurements.
scope note

Is defined by
https://purl.org/heals/eo

Example
What studies have backed this recommendation?
has super-classes

Sensorc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/Sensor

System that implements an ObservingProcedure to determine the value of an observable Property This may be a device, a piece of infrastructure, an agent (including humans), or software (simulation). A Sensor responds to a stimulus, e.g., a change in the environment, or input data composed from the results of prior Observations.
System that implements an ObservingProcedure to determine the value of an observable Property This may be a device, a piece of infrastructure, an agent (including humans), or software (simulation). A Sensor responds to a stimulus, e.g., a change in the environment, or input data composed from the results of prior Observations.
Alternative label
Observer
Is defined by
http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/obs/
Example
Accelerometers, gyroscopes, barometers, magnetometers, and so forth are Sensors that are typically mounted on a modern smartphone (which acts as Host or Platform). Other examples of Sensors include the human eyes.

Statistical explanationc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://purl.org/heals/eo#StatisticalExplanation

Presents an account of the outcome based on data about the occurrence of events under specified (e.g., experimental) conditions. Statistical explanations refer to numerical evidence on the likelihood of factors or processes influencing the result.

Systematic reviewc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: http://purl.org/spar/fabio/SystematicReview

A literature review focused on a single question that tries to identify, appraise, select and synthesize all high quality research evidence relevant to that question. Systematic reviews of high-quality randomized controlled trials are crucial to evidence-based medicine. An understanding of systematic reviews and how to implement them in practice is becoming mandatory for all professionals involved in the delivery of health care. Systematic reviews are not limited to medicine, and are quite common in other sciences such as psychology, educational research and sociology.
has super-classes
Review c

Unit of measurec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://saref.etsi.org/core/UnitOfMeasure

The unit of measure is a standard for measurement of a quantity, such as a Property. For example, Power is a property and Watt is a unit of power that represents a definite predetermined power: when we say 10 Watt, we actually mean 10 times the definite predetermined power called \"watt\". Our definition is based on the definition of unit of measure in the Ontology of units of Measure (OM). We propose here a list of some units of measure that are relevant for the purpose of SAREF, but this list can be extended, also using some other ontologies rather than the Ontology of units of Measure (OM).
Is defined by
https://saref.etsi.org/core/

is measured in op

References back to ToC

If you find the AFMO useful, please cite it as: ```bibtex @software{nzomo_afmo_2026, title = {Atrial Fibrillation Monitoring Ontology ({AFMO})}, author = {Nzomo, Mbithe}, version = {3.0}, year = {2026}, publisher = {Zenodo}, doi = {10.5281/zenodo.24157942}, url = {https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24157942}, } ``` If you use the general concepts, please cite the PHMO: ```bibtex @software{nzomo_phmo_2026, title = {Personal Health Monitoring Ontology ({PHMO})}, author = {Nzomo, Mbithe}, version = {1.0}, year = {2026}, publisher = {Zenodo}, doi = {10.5281/zenodo.24155503}, url = {https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24155503}, } ```

Changes since version 2.2 back to ToC

Version 3.0 separates the general personal health monitoring concepts of the AFMO into a new core ontology, the Personal Health Monitoring Ontology (PHMO) 1.0. The AFMO now imports the PHMO and defines the AF-specific concepts.

  • General classes, properties, and individuals moved from the afmo namespace to the phmo namespace. The renames file lists every old and new IRI.
  • afmo:ECG_sensor was renamed afmo:ECGSensor.
  • afmo:isHeavierThan and afmo:isLighterThan were renamed phmo:hasHigherBMIThan and phmo:hasLowerBMIThan.
  • The domain of hasSamplingFrequency was generalised from ECG observations to all continuous observations.
